title: Scoop a portion of fries into a fry carton at a fry dump station
instruction: Using the fry scoop, fill the small fry carton with a portion of fries from the station. Put the scoop back in the pan, leave the carton standing on the counter, and finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Fast food and counter workers (3,854,050 in the US, BLS OEWS May 2025) fill fry cartons all shift; O*NET 35-3023.00 lists "Select food items from serving or storage areas and place them in dishes, on serving trays, or in take-out bags." At a fry dump station the fries are taken with the station's scoop, never by hand, and tipped into a paper carton through the scoop's funnel end while the other hand holds the light carton, which a scoopful knocks over if it stands alone.
setup: A fast-food fry station in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A stainless-steel work counter 1 cm thick, from 10 to 90 cm forward, fixed. (2) A countertop fry dump station sized like the Avantco FFDS-1, fixed, all stainless: 33 cm wide, 57 cm deep and 49.5 cm tall, its front 21.5 cm forward, centred 15.5 cm left of the centre line. Its base, 7.3 cm tall with a control panel (heat and light switches, a pilot light), holds a full-size food pan 30 x 50.5 cm inside and 5.1 cm deep (floor 2.2 cm above the counter); a back panel carries a heat hood (two calrod elements and a lamp) 43 to 49.5 cm above the counter over the back 36 cm of the pan. (3) In the pan, 165 freshly fried straight-cut fries (9 mm square, 55 to 95 mm long, 5 g for 75 mm; 836 g in all, about a fryer-basket load), heaped from the scoop to the pan's back wall, about 6 cm high; 28 of them (141 g) lie in the scoop's front part, where they fell when the basket was dumped over it. (4) The station's fry scoop (polished stainless, 0.20 kg), lying flat in the front of the pan: a flat bottom 22.9 cm long that narrows from 20.3 cm across at its open end (toward the heap) to 9.5 cm at its open funnel end (toward the robot), side walls 5.7 cm tall, and a black cool-touch handle (12 cm long, 22 x 15 mm, rising 20 degrees) on its right wall at the funnel end, reaching out over the pan's right rim. (5) An empty small paper fry carton (red paperboard, 7.7 g): mouth 11.4 x 5.7 cm, base 8 x 3.4 cm, back 11.4 cm and low front 8.2 cm tall, standing on the counter 12.5 cm forward and 15.5 cm left of the centre line, its long side across, its low front toward the station. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0 at any time, and it stays 0: any part of the carton goes into the pan below its rim (the carton is not the scoop). A fry that a gripper or an arm touches is handled (PhysX contact view): it may not be served, and it counts as spilled wherever it lies. At the end of the trial: 0 if a handled fry is in the carton; 1.0 with 70 to 145 g of fries in the carton (from a kids' to a medium fast-food order, USDA FNDDS 71401030; a fry counts when its centre is inside the carton's walls, up to 2 cm above its back rim), the carton standing upright on the counter (tilted under 15 degrees, base within 5 mm of the counter), at most 4 fries spilled (about 20 g; outside both the pan and the carton, or handled), the scoop back in the pan (within 12 degrees of flat, its bottom within 3 cm of the pan's floor) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5 with 70 to 145 g in the standing carton; 0.25 with at least 30 g in the standing carton; else 0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the carton, the scoop and every fry still. Real trial: weigh the carton on a kitchen scale tared with an empty carton, count the fries on the counter and floor, and check from the video that the carton never went into the pan, that no fry the gripper touched went into the carton, that the carton stands and the scoop lies in the pan, and that the arms are back at their marks.
reset_notes: Tip the fries back into the pan, heap them against its back wall and over the scoop's open end with the scoop lying in the pan's front, and stand the empty carton back on its mark.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). Fries are rigid square sticks: no bending, breaking, oil or heat; friction 0.5 on each other, 0.6 on the pan, 0.55 on the scoop. The carton's 0.45 mm paperboard is modelled as rigid 3 mm walls at its real 7.7 g. The heat hood is drawn, not simulated. Robot-fry touches come from a PhysX contact view. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
